newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL says pipes almost back to full tilt.
newsitem.headline: IPL says pipes almost back to full tilt.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said Wednesday all its oil pipelines stretching to Ontario and the U.S. Midwest from western Canada had resumed pumping and full power was expected to be restored to Minnesota pumping units later today.

IPL spokesman Alan Roth said the system was moving about 1.15 million barrels per day, up from 860,000 late Tuesday, as utilities in Minnesota provided more power to pumping stations that were knocked off line in last weekend's brutal storm.
The company's target throughput for April was about 1.4 million barrels per day.

"Partial power in some cases, and full in other cases, has been restored to all but one of the pump stations that were down," Roth said. "And utilities in the region have indicated that full electrical service would be likely returned to all the stations today."
Volumes on the pipeline system, the world's longest for crude oil and petroleum products, were brought to a standstill last weekend when a power outage knocked out the pumping stations.

The company has been scrambling since Sunday to fix the situation which was made worse by the difficulty utilities have had in restoring power to their market regions following the snow-, ice- and windstorm.
The shutdown initially forced to a halt one million barrels of crude oil, which is equal to about half of Canada's total daily production.
"We're continuously working with shippers and we're still hoping to mitigate much of the impact on the industry customers by the end of the month," Roth said.
